SMTO-CFG-0012 — The Gateway couldn't start: its working folder path isn't a folder

GUID: df2bfbe4-0a23-47fb-8fc4-686f948552f4
Slug: gateway-config-gateway-workdir-is-not-a-directory
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer, stopped right after starting. Its working folder setting points to a file or something else that isn't a folder. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Copy the path from the error message and look at it on the Gateway's computer. Check whether it names a file rather than a folder. The message shows the exact path the Gateway tried to use as its working folder.
  2. Change GATEWAY_WORKDIR in the command or settings used to start the Gateway to the folder itself, for example by removing a file name at the end of the path. The Gateway runs commands inside this folder, so it must be a folder, not a file.
  3. Start the Gateway again. Then open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection on that Gateway. This shows whether the Gateway now starts with the corrected value and SMTO can reach it.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway keeps running after it starts, and in Settings › Setup › Gateways it shows Connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details (or copy the error shown where the Gateway was started) and send it, with the path, to the person who set up this Gateway. Don't delete or rename the file at that path to get past the error; it may be something you need.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway settings validation found that the configured workdir (GATEWAY_WORKDIR, or the Server's workspace root for the built-in LocalMachine Gateway) exists but is not a directory.

What this means

  • The configured Gateway workdir exists but is_dir() reports false. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • The configured Gateway workdir exists but is_dir() reports false.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact resolved path's resource type on the selected Gateway.

How to fix it

  • Set GATEWAY_WORKDIR to a directory (not a file, device or broken link target) that the Gateway's OS account can access, or replace the path with the intended directory; for the built-in LocalMachine Gateway the path is the Server's workspace root. Restart the Gateway afterwards.
  • Set GATEWAY_WORKDIR to an existing directory accessible by the Gateway service account. Restore the directory or its OS permissions before restarting the Gateway.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • GATEWAY_WORKDIR resolves to the intended accessible directory.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
